questions.stem: A sample of size n is to be selected from a population with population proportion p. For the sampling distribution of the sample proportion to be approximately normal, which of the following should be checked?
questions.answer_text: Proportions come from binomial distributions, and a binomial distribution will be approximately normal if n is large enough. We check that np and n(1 − p) are both ≥ 10. A sample size of at least 30 is a condition to be checked with regard to the sampling distribution of a sample mean. np and refer to the mean and standard deviation of a binomial distribution.

questions.stem: During a recent season, there were 560 players in the NBA. A sports statistician plans to sample 75 players randomly as to their views on whether they hope to stay with their current team for the rest of their career. Are all conditions for the sampling distribution of the sample proportion satisfied?
questions.answer_text: The 10% condition says that the sample size should be less than 10% of the population size. Here, the sample size of 75 is greater than 10% of the population size of 560.

questions.stem: In a study of a large number of patients arriving at a city hospital emergency room, the proportion of initial misdiagnoses was 0.14. The hospital typically averages between 100 and 200 emergency arrivals per day. Two simulations will be conducted for the sampling distribution of a sample proportion with a true proportion of 0.14. Simulation A will consist of 4,000 trials with a sample size of 100, while simulation B will consist of 2,000 trials with a sample size of 200. Which of the following statements correctly compares the center and variability of the two simulations?
questions.answer_text: The center of a sampling distribution for a population proportion equals the center of the distribution being sampled, so both distributions should be roughly centered at 0.14. The larger the sample size, the lesser the variability in the sampling distribution, so distribution B with a sample size of 200 will have less variability than distribution A with a sample size of 100.
